record.paper_title: Stellar models: firm evidence, open questions and future developments
record.context_brief: Predictive power of synthetic AGB models
record.original_question: What is the predictive power of synthetic Asymptotic Giant Branch models outside the parameter space covered by the populations used to calibrate them, given that these simulations still inherit the same unresolved physical problems as full evolutionary AGB models and require multiple parameters to be tuned by hand to match selected observations?

evidence.quote: As a consequence, in these synthetic simulations there is a number of free parameters that have to be tuned ‘by hand’ in order to reproduce some observational constraints such as for instance the Magellanic Clouds C-stars luminosity functions.

Synthetic AGB models constitute a much faster way to produce approximate models with these parameters tuned to match some observations, but it is not clear what their predictive power is, outside the parameter space covered by the calibrating AGB populations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Asymptotic Giant Branch (AGB) stars are evolved low- and intermediate-mass stars whose structure and chemical yields depend on physical processes (convective boundary mixing, third dredge-up efficiency, mass-loss rates, hot bottom burning, etc.) that are not yet determined from first principles. Two classes of models are used to describe AGB evolution:

(i) Full evolutionary AGB models, which integrate the stellar structure equations through the thermally pulsing phase but contain several unresolved physical uncertainties.

(ii) Synthetic AGB models, which parameterize the outcome of each thermal pulse and interpulse phase using analytic or fitted relations, with a finite collection of free parameters p = (p_1, …, p_n) (e.g., the minimum core mass for third dredge-up, the dredge-up efficiency lambda, mass-loss prescriptions, and HBB temperature). These free parameters are calibrated on a chosen set of observed AGB populations P_cal (for example, the carbon-star luminosity functions of the Magellanic Clouds), by selecting p so that model predictions reproduce the chosen observables.

Let Theta denote the full physical parameter space of an AGB star (initial mass, metallicity, mixing length, helium content, etc.), and let Theta_cal ⊂ Theta be the region populated by the calibration set P_cal.

Question: Quantify and characterize the predictive power of synthetic AGB models outside Theta_cal. Specifically, given that synthetic models inherit the same unresolved physical uncertainties as full evolutionary models and require hand-tuning of parameters p on P_cal, determine to what extent (and under what conditions on the parameterization, the choice of calibration observables, and the structure of Theta_cal) predictions made for points in Theta \ Theta_cal — such as integrated yields, surface chemical abundances, lifetimes, and luminosity functions for stellar populations at metallicities, ages, or initial-mass ranges not represented in P_cal — remain reliable.
artifact.status_search_result: This is an open scientific modeling question rather than a closed mathematical problem. The literature on synthetic AGB models (e.g., Marigo & Girardi, Cristallo et al., Karakas, Pastorelli et al.) continues to refine calibrations using Magellanic Cloud and Milky Way data, but the extrapolation reliability of synthetic AGB models outside calibrated regions remains acknowledged as an unresolved issue, and recalibrations are repeatedly needed when new observational datasets (e.g., from JWST, Gaia, or new MC surveys) become available.

status_evidence.title: Constraining the thermally pulsing AGB phase with resolved stellar populations in the SMC (Pastorelli et al.)
status_evidence.snippet: We calibrate the TP-AGB models … free parameters tuned to reproduce the observed star counts and luminosity functions in the SMC.
status_evidence.claim: Synthetic/parameterized AGB models continue to require recalibration against new resolved-population data, indicating ongoing uncertainty in extrapolation.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotic Giant Branch stars: modelling and observations (Karakas review)
status_evidence.snippet: Significant uncertainties remain in the modelling of AGB stars, particularly regarding mass loss, third dredge-up and convective mixing.
status_evidence.claim: Underlying physical uncertainties of AGB modelling persist, supporting that synthetic-model predictive power outside calibration regions is not established.
